narrative:
The Karnataka High Court recorded a total of 1,062 cases heard out of 2,723 scheduled for November 24, 2026, resulting in a hearing rate of 39.0%. This maintains the trajectory observed on November 23 (38.4%) but remains lower than the performance levels seen earlier in the week, such as November 20 (45.1%). The gap in hearing rates between government and commoner cases was narrow, at 2.2%, with government cases heard at a 40.6% rate and commoner cases at 38.4%.

Judge-wise performance showed high variability. K. V. Aravind (Hall 34) exhibited a significant disparity, with a high conversion rate of 95.7% for a specific bench segment, while other segments in the same hall saw lower activity. Other notable throughputs included Geetha K.B. (Hall 35), who maintained an 85.7% hearing rate on a portion of her list, and Anu Sivaraman (Hall 2), who achieved a 73.2% rate. Conversely, several benches, including Suraj Govindaraj (Hall 13) and Anu Sivaraman & K.S. Bharath Kumar (Hall 2), reported no cases heard from their scheduled lists.

Hearing stage conversion metrics indicate that "Orders" led the volume with 410 cases heard (46.6% conversion), followed by "Admission" (34.5%) and "Preliminary Hearing" (42.4%). "Final Hearing" stages continue to record the lowest conversion at 25.1%, consistent with the historical context of the preceding days.

Case type distribution was dominated by Writ Petitions (WP), with 436 heard out of 1,255 scheduled (34.7%). While WP hearing rates improved slightly compared to November 23 (32.9%), they remained below the 45.8% observed on November 19. Criminal Revision Petitions (CRL.RP) exhibited the highest clearance efficiency among primary types at 75.4%, significantly outpacing the overall bench performance.
